blocks.content: The State Executive consists of the Governor, the Chief Minister, the Council of Ministers, and the Advocate General of the State.

rows: Appointed by the President of India
Acts on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers
Heads the Council of Ministers and directs government policy

items: Examiners frequently test whether the Advocate General is part of the State Executive (Yes, unlike the CAG who is not part of Union Executive).
Remember that there is NO office of Vice-Governor in Indian states.
Articles 153 to 167 in Part VI are often matched with their respective executive functions in Prelims MCQs.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Articles 153 to 167 in Part VI of the Indian Constitution deal with the State Executive.
The State Executive comprises the Governor, the Chief Minister, the Council of Ministers, and the Advocate General of the State.
There is no provision for the office of Vice-Governor in the Indian state political system.
The Governor is the constitutional (de jure) head of the state, whereas the Chief Minister is the real (de facto) executive head.
The Advocate General serves as the highest law officer in the state and is an integral part of the State Executive.
